# CRT: see libcxxabi/recipe.json's own matching patch note -- MINGW_LIBRARIES
# names a real mingw-w64 distribution's own CRT stub import libraries this
# project's sysroot has never had and will never provide (this project's
# --target=*-w64-mingw32 is ABI-compatibility-only; tools/crt-c++ already
# supplies the real link line). Deliberately no-op'd -- do not re-add.
patches.reason: Same as libcxxabi/recipe.json's matching patch: confirmed for real ("lld: error: unable to find library -lmingw32" and 15 siblings) building libc++abi first; applying the identical fix here preemptively since libcxx's own lib/CMakeLists.txt has the exact same line.

Confirmed for real: 6 libcxx source files (algorithm.cpp, chrono.cpp, iostream.cpp, ios.cpp, locale.cpp, random.cpp) fail with 'fatal error: xlocinfo.h file not found' via this exact locale_win32.h include -- xlocinfo.h is a real Universal CRT header this freestanding -nostdinc build cannot provide, and implementing its real _locale_t/_create_locale/_X_l function family would mean linking ucrtbase.dll. Redirecting to locale_bionic.h instead uses this project's own already-implemented Bionic-compatible locale_t/newlocale/xlocale.h surface (libc/src/locale.c, include/xlocale.h) -- verified to already cover nearly everything locale.cpp calls (locale_t, newlocale/uselocale/freelocale, strcoll_l/strftime_l/strxfrm_l/tolower_l/toupper_l/towlower_l/towupper_l/wcscoll_l/wcsxfrm_l, the full iswctype_l family).

Same root cause and same fix shape as the __locale patch above, for a completely independent feature: random_device's Windows path (_LIBCPP_USING_WIN32_RANDOM, selected via _LIBCPP_WIN32API which this project correctly keeps defined for chrono.cpp's own legitimate Windows-native timing APIs) calls rand_s(), a real Universal CRT function requiring _CRT_RAND_S and ucrtbase.dll -- not yet hit as a build failure (random.cpp's current failure is the earlier __locale-driven one), but would be the very next gap once that is fixed. Pre-empting it here since the fix is a one-line exclusion and the fallback path is already fully implemented in this project's own libc.

Confirmed for real: once the #include-selection patch above took effect, __locale's own __libcpp_locale_guard struct still picked the _LIBCPP_MSVCRT_LIKE branch (guarded by !defined(_LIBCPP_LOCALE__L_EXTENSIONS), which __config's own _LIBCPP_LOCALE__L_EXTENSIONS definition sets true whenever _LIBCPP_MSVCRT_LIKE is true, unconditionally, regardless of the #include patch) -- 'use of undeclared identifier _ENABLE_PER_THREAD_LOCALE'/'_configthreadlocale' and 'incomplete definition of type struct __crt_locale' (locale_t's pointee is intentionally opaque in this project's own locale.h, exactly as real Bionic's is -- the MSVC branch dereferences it directly, which only a real MSVC _locale_t struct layout could support).

Confirmed for real: ctype_base::mask's own separate _LIBCPP_MSVCRT_LIKE branch (real MSVC ctype.h bitmask macros _SPACE/_BLANK/_PUNCT/_ALPHA/_DIGIT/_CONTROL/_UPPER/_LOWER/_HEX, none of which this project declares) is a THIRD, independent _LIBCPP_MSVCRT_LIKE decision point in this same header, unrelated to both patches above. Excluding __BIONIC__ here needs no new branch of our own: falling through lands on this same chain's final, fully self-contained #else (plain `1<<0`/`1<<1`/... bit values, no host ctype.h dependency at all) -- exactly what real Android/Bionic (which this chain also never names explicitly) already relies on today.
Scoped the same way as the ctype_base::mask patch above: this project's own errno.h (not MSVC stdlib.h's _sys_nerr) is the correct include for the _LIBCPP_ELAST selection immediately below.

Confirmed this project's own libc has no _sys_nerr (an old MSVC/mingw CRT global, never a Bionic one either -- real Android's own libcxx port does not define _LIBCPP_ELAST at all, matching the #else '#warning ELAST for this platform not yet implemented' branch this exclusion now falls through to for us). Not yet confirmed as an actual build failure (config_elast.h was never reached before the __locale patches above), but the same _sys_nerr gap the other three patches in this recipe were all written to avoid, so fixed alongside them rather than waiting for a separate build cycle to rediscover it.

A fifth, independent _LIBCPP_MSVCRT_LIKE-family branch point, missed by grepping for _LIBCPP_MSVCRT_LIKE/_LIBCPP_MSVCRT alone because this one is spelled differently: locale.cpp's own #include picks the win32 backend whenever EITHER _LIBCPP_MSVCRT OR __MINGW32__ is defined -- and __MINGW32__ is unconditionally defined by Clang for this project's --target=x86_64-w64-mingw32 (confirmed via clang++ -dM -E), independent of _LIBCPP_MSVCRT_LIKE/_LIBCPP_MSVCRT entirely. Confirmed for real: 'fatal error: xlocinfo.h file not found' via locale.cpp:33 even after every __locale-side patch above was applied. The existing #elif !defined(__BIONIC__) already shows upstream itself anticipated a __BIONIC__ case here (falling through to nothing at all, since this project's own <locale.h>/<xlocale.h> already supply everything __locale's generic path needs) -- this patch only needed to make the FIRST branch stop shadowing that intent for a Bionic target that also happens to define __MINGW32__.

Confirmed for real: 'no member named strerror_s in the global namespace' -- a sixth independent _LIBCPP_MSVCRT_LIKE branch point, this one selecting between a real Universal CRT strerror_s() and a portable strerror_r()-based do_strerror_r() (the #else branch immediately below, unconditionally available since this project's own libc implements POSIX strerror_r). Same exclusion pattern as every other patch in this recipe.

# CRT: src/support/win32/{support,thread_win32,locale_win32}.cpp implement
# the MSVC-locale-backend's own internal helpers (vsnprintf_l/errno_t/
# wcrtomb_s/_create_locale/...) this recipe's own __locale/locale.cpp/
# system_error.cpp patches (see this file's own patches above) already
# redirect entirely away from -- they are unconditionally CMake-globbed
# in whenever WIN32 is true, with no way to select them out from the
# preprocessor side the way every other MSVCRT_LIKE branch in this recipe
# was excluded. Deliberately no-op'd at the CMake level instead, the same
# discipline this recipe already applies to upstream's own if(MINGW)
# blocks elsewhere: real MSVC Universal CRT symbols these three files
# need (errno_t, _create_locale, wcrtomb_s, vasprintf_l, ...) this
# project does not have and does not want, so nothing should try to
# compile them at all rather than papering over each one with more
# shim declarations.
if(FALSE)
  file(GLOB LIBCXX_WIN32_SOURCES ../src/support/win32/*.cpp)
  list(APPEND LIBCXX_SOURCES ${LIBCXX_WIN32_SOURCES})
elseif("${CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME}" STREQUAL "SunOS")
patches.reason: Confirmed for real: even after every source-level MSVCRT_LIKE redirect in __locale/locale.cpp/system_error.cpp above, lib/CMakeLists.txt's own `if(WIN32) file(GLOB ... ../src/support/win32/*.cpp)` unconditionally compiles support.cpp/thread_win32.cpp/locale_win32.cpp regardless of what any header selects -- 'use of undeclared identifier _vsnprintf/errno_t/wcrtomb_s/_create_locale/vasprintf_l', 'process.h file not found' (thread_win32.cpp). These files are genuinely dead code for this project once the redirects above are in place: nothing else references anything they define.

patches.replace:
# the dylib when get ODR used by another function.
#
# CRT: -fvisibility-inlines-hidden is safe on ELF/Mach-O (macOS, Linux):
# a client TU can still freely emit its own local copy of a hidden-
# visibility inline function (e.g. basic_string::size()/data()), since
# ELF/Mach-O visibility only controls cross-DSO export, never whether a
# client may define the symbol itself. On a Windows/PE shared build it is
# NOT safe: this recipe's own client (tests/imported_libcxx_test.cc,
# linked shared) sees extern template class __declspec(dllimport)
# basic_string<char> (via _LIBCPP_EXTERN_TEMPLATE_TYPE_VIS), which
# forbids the client from defining ANY of its members locally --
# including the hidden-visibility inline ones -fvisibility-inlines-
# hidden causes Clang to emit real -exclude-symbols .drectve directives
# for inside libc++.dll itself (confirmed for real: dumped the .drectve
# section of the compiled src/string.cpp.obj and found `-exclude-
# symbols:` entries for exactly the mangled names -- size()/data()/
# __init()/... -- lld-link later reported undefined for). The two
# project policies contradict on Windows only: "hide inline
# implementation details from the export table" versus "the client is
# never allowed to supply them locally either." Disabling the flag for
# Windows only lets libc++.dll's own real dllexport annotation (from
# _LIBCPP_CLASS_TEMPLATE_INSTANTIATION_VIS on the explicit template
# instantiation, unaffected by this flag) govern the export table
# instead.
if (NOT WIN32)
  add_compile_flags_if_supported(-fvisibility-inlines-hidden)
endif()
patches.reason: Confirmed for real: crt-libcxx-smoke's *shared* leg failed with dozens of 'undefined symbol: __declspec(dllimport) std::__1::basic_string<...>::size() const' (and ~15 siblings: data(), __init(), append(), the destructor, __vector_base_common, ...) even though src/string.cpp's own explicit template instantiation (template class _LIBCPP_CLASS_TEMPLATE_INSTANTIATION_VIS basic_string<char>;) genuinely compiles every one of those members as a real, external (T) symbol -- confirmed via llvm-nm on the compiled object. Part one of two real, independent causes (see the include/__config patch just below for the second, which turned out to be the one that actually mattered): -fvisibility-inlines-hidden (unconditionally applied by libcxx's own top-level CMakeLists.txt) makes Clang auto-generate .drectve -exclude-symbols directives for _LIBCPP_INLINE_VISIBILITY-marked (hidden-visibility) members -- confirmed by dumping string.cpp.obj's own .drectve section before and after this patch (present, then gone). Disabling it was necessary but not sufficient on its own: the undefined-symbol errors persisted identically even with a freshly rebuilt, exclude-symbols-free object, which is what led to finding the include/__config mismatch. The static leg was never affected by either: -D_LIBCPP_DISABLE_VISIBILITY_ANNOTATIONS (tools/crt-c++) already makes the client side a non-issue there.

The actual, deeper cause of the shared-leg undefined-symbol failures the patch above only partially addressed: confirmed via the exact 'dllexport attribute ignored ... missing on previous declaration' compiler warning naming basic_string<char>/basic_iostream<char> by name, and via the undefined-symbol errors persisting identically even after string.cpp.obj's own .drectve exclude-symbols list was confirmed empty (a fresh rebuild after the -fvisibility-inlines-hidden fix). This is a real, narrow LLVM libcxx source patch, not a CMake-option/recipe-metadata change -- necessary because this project's own dedicated crt-libcxx-build.py engine has no equivalent of a real LLVM Windows toolchain's own additional export-list-generation machinery (if any exists) that might otherwise route around this mismatch.

patches.replace:
install(TARGETS ${LIBCXX_INSTALL_TARGETS} ${filesystem_lib} ${experimental_lib}
    LIBRARY DESTINATION ${LIBCXX_INSTALL_PREFIX}lib${LIBCXX_LIBDIR_SUFFIX} COMPONENT cxx
    ARCHIVE DESTINATION ${LIBCXX_INSTALL_PREFIX}lib${LIBCXX_LIBDIR_SUFFIX} COMPONENT cxx
    # CRT: upstream's own install(TARGETS) here never names a RUNTIME
    # DESTINATION at all -- harmless on ELF/Mach-O (a shared object is a
    # LIBRARY artifact there, never a RUNTIME one), but on Windows/PE a
    # shared library target produces BOTH an ARCHIVE artifact (the
    # libc++.dll.a import library, already installed above) AND a
    # separate RUNTIME artifact (the actual libc++.dll) -- and CMake
    # silently skips installing an artifact kind with no destination
    # given, rather than defaulting it. Confirmed for real: crt-libcxx-
    # smoke's shared leg linked clean (this recipe's other two patches
    # above fixed the export-table gap) but the resulting .exe exited
    # 3221225781 (0xC0000135 / STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND) at *run* time --
    # `cmake --install` never copied libc++.dll into install/bin at all,
    # only libc++.a/libc++.dll.a/libc++experimental.a made it to
    # install/lib. libunwind's own upstream src/CMakeLists.txt already
    # gets this right (a sibling RUNTIME DESTINATION ${LIBUNWIND_INSTALL_
    # RUNTIME_DIR} clause), confirmed via install/bin/libunwind.dll
    # actually existing -- this patch brings libcxx's own install rule up
    # to the same shape.
    RUNTIME DESTINATION ${LIBCXX_INSTALL_PREFIX}bin COMPONENT cxx
    )
patches.reason: Confirmed for real, as the second of two genuinely separate shared-leg root causes found this pass: after the export-table fix above, crt-libcxx-smoke's shared .exe LINKS clean (no more undefined dllimport symbols) but FAILS TO RUN with STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND, because libc++.dll itself (as opposed to its libc++.dll.a import library) was never installed to install/bin -- confirmed by direct inspection: install/bin held only libunwind.dll, while build/libcxx/lib/libc++.dll existed in the raw build tree but was never copied out by `cmake --install`. Root-caused to this install(TARGETS) call never specifying a RUNTIME DESTINATION, which CMake requires per-artifact-kind (unlike LIBRARY/ARCHIVE, a missing RUNTIME DESTINATION means that artifact kind is simply never installed, not defaulted to somewhere sensible) -- verified by direct comparison against libunwind's own working src/CMakeLists.txt, which does include a RUNTIME DESTINATION clause and does get its .dll installed correctly every time.

notes: dependencies now includes libunwind directly (previously transitive only, through libcxxabi), and target_overrides.windows.options links libunwind's shared import library into libc++.dll's own CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS -- the exact same fix, for the exact same reason, as ../libcxxabi/recipe.json's own matching entry: confirmed for real via 'ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: _Unwind_Resume' (and 376 more references) the first time cxx_shared/libc++.dll's own link was actually reached. A Windows DLL must resolve every referenced symbol at its own link time, unlike an ELF .so; libc++.dll pulls in libc++abi's exception-unwind call chain transitively through -lc++abi, but that does not itself re-export libunwind's symbols to libc++.dll's own link step.

The Bionic locale/random backend redirect (the __locale/__config/locale.cpp/system_error.cpp/lib-CMakeLists.txt patches above) was a deliberate, investigated decision, not a quick workaround -- see TODO.md's C++ runtime prerequisite section and HISTORY.md's dated entry for the full writeup of why (avoids linking the hosted Universal CRT ucrtbase.dll, matching this project's 'own the toolchain' principle already applied to libunwind/exceptions) and what it took (six independent _LIBCPP_MSVCRT_LIKE-family branch points across __locale/__config/locale.cpp/system_error.cpp, one CMake-level glob exclusion for now-dead src/support/win32/*.cpp files, and three new win32_shim declarations -- __int64, SYSTEM_INFO/GetSystemInfo, FILETIME/LARGE_INTEGER/QueryPerformance*/GetSystemTime*AsFileTime -- for the legitimate Windows-native chrono.cpp/thread.cpp code paths this redirect deliberately leaves alone).

target_overrides.windows.build_targets omits cxx_filesystem: libcxx's own top-level CMakeLists.txt sets ENABLE_FILESYSTEM_DEFAULT OFF specifically `if (WIN32)` (LIBCXX_ENABLE_FILESYSTEM defaults ON, matching LIBCXX_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_LIBRARY, everywhere else), so the cxx_filesystem CMake target this recipe's common build_targets requests is simply never generated on Windows -- 'ninja: error: unknown target cxx_filesystem', not a soft skip. This project deliberately does not override LIBCXX_ENABLE_FILESYSTEM back to ON for Windows: upstream's own WIN32-specific default is left as-is (no stated rationale found in the fetched source to second-guess), and nothing in this project currently exercises <filesystem>, so build_targets is adjusted to match what Windows's own CMake configuration actually offers instead. macOS and Linux both keep the common list unchanged, matching their own already-verified crt-libcxx-smoke runs.

LIBCXX_STANDARD_VER=c++14: Android's own build uses a newer dialect than this legacy standalone CMake default; keeping this cache value also avoids the removed C11 gets() import while preserving the public CRT headers.

LIBCXX_HAS_RT_LIB=OFF on every host: modern Bionic provides the historical librt surface from libc itself. The standalone libc++ probe is also compiled as a static library and can report a false positive without performing a real link, so this is pinned off everywhere rather than leaking a host librt dependency into Linux.

post_install_copy.macos stages libc++'s own upstream not-weak symbol-export policy list (lib/notweak.exp) into the shared install prefix as libc++.notweak.exp -- tools/crt-c++'s macOS static-link path applies it via -Wl,-force_symbols_not_weak_list so a stray host libSystem symbol can never interpose this project's own C++ allocator.

extra_files' src/__crt_dso_handle.cpp mirrors libcxxabi/recipe.json's own shim of the identical name/content -- and is NOT a duplicate of it. Per the Itanium C++ ABI, __dso_handle identifies one specific DSO/shared-object image; libcxxabi's copy exists so *its own* static-init-guard code has one, and libcxx needs its *own separate* copy for the exact same reason (src/debug.cpp's __get_db() references it directly). This project's own crt1.o never defines __dso_handle at all (Bionic's real crtbegin/crtend split is not imported), so nothing else provides it here. No CMakeLists.txt patch is needed the way libcxxabi's shim required one: libcxx's own lib/CMakeLists.txt already does `file(GLOB LIBCXX_SOURCES ../src/*.cpp)`, which picks up this new file automatically. Found for real (2026-08-21) as a linker fixup error building libc++.dylib on macOS aarch64 -- 'ld: fixup error (kind=arm64_adrp_lo12) ... target ___dso_handle does not have address' -- confirmed via nm that debug.cpp.o carried an undefined ___dso_handle with no definition anywhere in libcxx's own build, unlike libcxxabi which already had its shim; see HISTORY.md.
